### 2.4 - The Distributive Property

:::{.answers}

23. 

    Distribute first:

    $$
    \begin{aligned}
    4(2x + 3) - (2x + 3) &= \\
    4(2x) + 4(3) -1(2x) -1(3) &= \\
    8x + 12 - 2x - 3 &= 6x + 9
    \end{aligned}
    $$

    Factor first:
    $$
    \begin{aligned}
    4(2x + 3) - (2x + 3) &= \\
    (4 - 1) * (2x + 3) &= \\
    3 (2x + 3) & = 6x + 9
    \end{aligned}
    $$

    These are equivalent because the distributive property works both ways. We can expand by multiplying into parentheses or we can factor out by pulling out what's common. In both cases, we are just rearranging the same multiplication and subtraction.

24. 

    You have to distribute twice.

    $$
    \begin{aligned}
    (3x - 1) * (2x + 3) &= \\
    (3x - 1)(2x) + (3x - 1)(-1) &= \\
    6x^2 - 2x - 3x + 1 &= 6x^2 -5x + 1
    \end{aligned}
    $$

:::

### 2.6 - Equivalent Expressions

:::{.answers}

24. $3(x+k)=3x+3k=3x+12 \Rightarrow k=4$.

25. Factor out an $x+2$ from $E_1(x)$

    $$
    \begin{aligned}
    E_1(x) &= (x+2)(4x-1) + 3(x+2) \\
    &= (x+2)((4x - 1) + 3) \\
    &= (x + 2) (4x + 2) \\
    &= 2(x + 2)(2x + 1)
    \end{aligned}
    $$

    The expressions are equivalent.
:::

### 4.2 - Understanding Slope

:::{.answers}

24. $m_1=3,\ m_2=-\tfrac{1}{3}$
    Their product is $m_1 m_2 = 3\cdot(-\tfrac{1}{3})=-1$.
    Slopes that are **negative reciprocals** correspond to **perpendicular lines**, so the lines are perpendicular.

25. Original line through origin and $(x,y)$ has slope $m=\frac{y}{x}$.
    If the slope doubles, $m' = 2m = \frac{2y}{x}$.
    For a new point $(x',y')$ on the doubled-slope line through the origin, we need
    
    $$
    \frac{y'}{x'}= \frac{2y}{x}.
    $$

    Keeping the same $x$ (i.e., $x'=x$) forces $y'=2y$.
    **Conclusion:** doubling the slope (with the same $x$) doubles the vertical change. The line becomes twice as steep by stretching the $y$-values while $x$ stays fixed.
    
:::

### 6.7 - Applications of Quadratics

:::{.answers}

11. Example situation: the height of an object thrown upward.
    The vertex represents the maximum height and when it occurs.

12. Zeros at $t=0$ and $t=5$:
    $$
    h(t)=a t(t-5)
    $$
    Vertex time is midpoint:
    $$
    t=\frac{0+5}{2}=2.5
    $$
    Given maximum height $64$ at $t=2.5$:
    $$
    64=a(2.5)(-2.5)=a(-6.25)
    $$
    $$
    a=-\frac{64}{6.25}=-\frac{256}{25}
    $$
    One possible model:
    $$
    h(t)=-\frac{256}{25}t(t-5)
    $$
:::
